plan.G: After research closes, select only correctly validated candidates and test any proposed combinations afresh. Compare each combination against its inputs and the baseline using the official geometric-mean kernel-time objective; do not assume gains are additive. Independently confirm the best candidate, and retain the best independently confirmed program if no candidate improves on the baseline. Do not launch further research trees during assembly.
plan.analysis: Choose N=3: the supplied kernel repeatedly evaluates all-pairs interactions, so the useful opportunities are source-data reuse, target work granularity, and interaction arithmetic. These are distinct optimization axes; more trees would risk duplicating them. The baseline is valid and reports three search timings with a mean of 0.001844410 seconds (score 0.5); the supplied data does not expose per-size timings, so it does not establish which size dominates. All trees must preserve the specified interface and particle layout, produce complete outputs with masses unchanged, and pass the full correctness protocol, including small sizes, coincident positions, zero or negative dt, and the extreme-mass case. Judge candidates by the official geometric mean across N=4096, 8192, and 16384, not by an isolated timing.

children.objective: Explore CTA-level shared-memory tiling of source particles for the all-pairs loop, reusing each staged source across output particles. Handle partial tiles and output bounds correctly for all tested sizes, and keep shared-memory use within the allowed limit. Work only in src/nbody_kernel.cu and src/launch.json. Measure the memory-reuse and occupancy tradeoff under the official protocol; retain only variants that pass all correctness checks.
children.subject: Shared-memory source tiling

children.objective: Explore output coarsening: have threads or blocks compute multiple distinct target particles, reusing source values in registers and adjusting block/items_per_block consistently with the harness grid mapping. Do not use shared-memory source tiling in this tree, so its results isolate target granularity and launch geometry. Ensure every output is written exactly once, including partial target groups; preserve all interface and correctness requirements. Measure all three scored sizes with the official protocol.
children.subject: Register reuse through target coarsening and launch geometry

children.objective: Explore arithmetic restructuring of the direct one-target-per-thread source loop, such as algebraically canceling the positive target mass from the acceleration expression and evaluating reciprocal-square-root-based interaction factors. Avoid shared-memory tiling and multi-target coarsening so the measurements isolate arithmetic changes. Treat changed floating-point ordering or approximation as a correctness risk: validate against the full GPU tolerance and independent FP64 checks, including coincident positions and the extreme-mass case, before comparing official timings.

data.analysis: T1 and T2 are not identical mechanisms, but their broad objectives both pursue source reuse; T2 also permits block-level coarsening, so it could overlap T1. In the supplied loop, lanes in a warp use the same j, making each source address uniform across lanes. Staging may still help, but reduced traffic is unproven and staging has costs. Narrow T1 to one target per thread and T2 to per-thread register coarsening without shared memory. A contrasting direct-loop experiment is also missing: retain self-exclusion while testing split source ranges to avoid the per-j self check, alongside isolated arithmetic variants. The extreme-mass test makes preserving self-exclusion important. The only performance evidence available here is the baseline; no candidate measurements settle these hypotheses.

revisions.objective: Explore CTA-level shared-memory tiling of source particles, with exactly one target per thread and no multi-target coarsening. Use a consistent mapping such as items_per_block=block, stage source tiles, and handle partial tiles and output bounds. Keep shared-memory use within the allowed limit. Compare staging costs and benefits under the official protocol; pass all correctness checks before timing. Work only in src/nbody_kernel.cu and src/launch.json.
revisions.subject: Shared-memory source tiling with one target per thread

revisions.objective: Explore per-thread register coarsening only: each thread computes multiple distinct target particles while reusing source values in registers. Do not use shared-memory source tiling or block-level multi-output assignment, so this contrasts with T1. Set block and items_per_block to implement an explicit, unique target mapping (for example, items_per_block as a multiple of block); handle partial groups and write each output exactly once. Measure the reuse, register-pressure, and parallelism tradeoffs across all scored sizes under the official protocol, after full correctness checks.
revisions.subject: Per-thread target coarsening without shared memory

revisions.objective: Explore direct-loop control and arithmetic changes with one target per thread, no shared-memory tiling, and no multi-target coarsening. Contrast the original self-exclusion check with split source ranges that exclude j=i without evaluating that interaction; do not simply include the self term, since intermediate overflow could make a zero-displacement term non-finite for extreme mass. Separately test arithmetic variants such as target-mass cancellation or reciprocal-square-root-based factors, first in isolation and then in useful combinations. Validate against the GPU tolerance and FP64 checks, including coincident positions and extreme mass, before timing all scored sizes under the official protocol.
revisions.subject: Direct-loop control and arithmetic

data.shared_assumptions: The three topics retain the direct all-pairs kernel as the optimization baseline. T1/T2 assume source reuse might help, but source indices are uniform across warp lanes, so reduced traffic from staging or coarsening is unproven. Coarsening and shared memory may also trade against parallelism or occupancy. Loop and arithmetic changes must preserve self-exclusion and pass reference and oracle checks; the supplied baseline is not evidence that any candidate wins.
